title: Replacing a Leaking PVC Sink Trap: Cut, Remove, and Rebuild the Kitchen Drain

locations.name: Under kitchen sink (probable filming location in cabinet)
locations.basis: Transcript references the kitchen sink drain and the trap located under the sink; no explicit shooting location is stated.

summary: This Old House demonstrates diagnosing a leaking PVC sink trap and replacing a glued, in-wall drain run with a new, correctly sized assembly. The video explains why glued PVC joints must be cut out rather than unsoldered, shows how to drain and remove the old trap, uses a drill-mounted cutter head to extract remaining in-wall pipe, and then fabricates a new drainage run that reduces from a 2-inch wall pipe to a 1.5-inch trap. The sequence includes dry-fitting in a tight cabinet, gluing the wall connection, assembling compression fittings, and testing the finished install with a bowl and paper towel to verify a watertight connection.

sections.title: Identify leak and plan removal
concepts: need to cut out damaged section
sections.description: The presenter notes a leaking PVC trap after final inspection and explains that PVC joints are glued and cannot be unsoldered, necessitating cutting out the damaged assembly.

sections.title: Remove old glued assembly and clear in-wall pipe
concepts: special cutter head with guide disc
sections.description: The old assembly is taken apart by cutting at the base of the Y; remaining in-wall PVC is removed with a drill-mounted cutter head designed to avoid damaging fittings.

sections.title: Fabricate and install new drain run; test
concepts: water test with bowl and paper towel
sections.description: A new run is assembled with a 2-inch wall pipe reduced to 1.5-inch to fit the trap; joints are glued after cleaning, parts are dry-fitted in a tight space, and compression connections are completed before a water test verifies watertightness.
